title: An Empirical Preregistered Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for Intent-to-Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) that compares LLM-only configuration generation to a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent-to-configuration NetOps tasks. Using a frozen plan, a Dockerized Mininet emulation, a deterministic validator, and gpt-5-mini, we ran 200 stratified paired trials (5 protocol groups × 2 modalities × ≈20 tasks) with fully archived artifacts and hashes. Observed outcomes: baseline (LLM-only) = 200/200 verifier-accepted configurations; GVR = 200/200. The paired difference in the operational-failure indicator = 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.00]; bootstrap resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729); Wilcoxon two-sided p = 1.0. The preregistered power assumption (baseline failure > 0) was not met; therefore the confirmatory null outcome reflects the tested scope (synthetic vendor-like templates, Mininet emulation, single model, deterministic validator) rather than a general claim that GVR is unnecessary in broader operational settings. We publish full execution and analysis artifacts, deterministic reconciliations, and the immutable initial master-prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: LLMs are proposed to automate NetOps tasks (intent-to-configuration) but can produce operationally unsafe outputs. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipelines are widely advocated to bound risk by adding deterministic validation and limited repair loops. We preregistered (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) a paired experiment that asks: does GVR measurably reduce operational-failure rates (reachability loss or policy violation) relative to LLM-only generation under a controlled, artifact-backed evaluation?
sections.related_work: Benchmarks and evaluations of LLMs for NetOps include NetConfEval (Wang et al., 2024), OpsEval (Liu et al., 2023), and NetEval (Miao et al., 2023), which motivate structured task banks and verifier-assisted pipelines. Prior architectural proposals advocate verifier-assisted generation and GVR loops; ours contributes a fully preregistered paired design with deterministic artifacts and public hashes to clarify boundary conditions where GVR yields measurable benefit.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The machine-readable preregistration (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) froze the research question, estimands, sampling plan (n=200 paired confirmatory tasks), metrics, validator policy, retry policy, contamination thresholds, and analysis plan (paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed=1729; Wilcoxon exact test). Execution harness. Adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256 a40e96e2...). Tasks and testbed. Confirmatory bank: 200 intent-to-configuration tasks stratified over 5 protocol groups and two interaction modalities (CLI, API); tasks were synthetic but vendor-inspired and deterministic (task_manifest.jsonl, see execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256 c1bd4a09...). Emulation validator. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is the operational oracle: it parses generated configurations, normalizes commands, enforces declared workflow policies (e.g., "must be down for MTU/VLAN change", minimum-up constraints), executes syntactic and semantic checks in a Dockerized Mininet emulation, runs reachability probes and policy/ACL checks, and reports violations. The transformation/validator artifact manifest is in execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA-256 7925b8f25adbb269b3f2099ae3d96c2bc436a7f31011b067210a2c7f73bb63fb). Shared-generation semantics. Per the preregistration the generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): a single LLM-produced candidate was stored and evaluated under both arms (baseline and guarded) for each task. This choice is recorded in the preregistration and the execution manifest; it implies baseline and guarded responses may be identical when no repair is invoked (see Results). Contamination checks. A deterministic contamination detector flagged generated outputs with ≥80% token overlap vs curated public corpora; no confirmatory tasks exceeded the threshold (contamination_summary.csv, execution artifact).
sections.results: Execution and primary outcomes. All planned calls completed (planned model-call budget = 400; model_calls_used = 200; no infrastructure failures). Confirmatory counts: complete paired tasks = 200; baseline success (verifier-accepted) = 200/200; guarded success = 200/200. Paired contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); Wilcoxon signed-rank exact p = 1.0. Deterministic reconciliation checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Representative artifacts. Execution manifest contains full response files and hashes (examples: task-000001 response hash f8de4d6e..., task-000002 hash ae967f70...; all baseline and guarded response hashes are identical across conditions for every task—see execution/execution_manifest.json artifact hashes and the representative scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/). Contamination and exclusions. Contamination detector flagged 0 confirmatory tasks; no exclusions occurred.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and bounds. The preregistered hypothesis (H1) expected a measurable paired reduction via GVR; it is not supported in this specific controlled setting because baseline already succeeded on all tasks. Key reasons (artifact-backed): (1) shared_initial_candidate semantics and deterministic validator: the experiment used a single LLM candidate per task that was evaluated in both arms; no repairs were invoked, so baseline and guarded outcomes coincided (manifest evidences and identical response hashes). (2) Task and validator scope: the confirmatory bank used synthetic, vendor-like templates and a deterministic validator that enforces explicit workflow constraints and reachability probes; these conditions reduced the opportunity for divergence. (3) single-model, single-seed design: only gpt-5-mini was tested; other models or higher generation stochasticity could produce different outcomes. Consequence for power and inference. The preregistered power calculation targeted detection of a 10 percentage-point absolute reduction; this assumed baseline nonzero failure rate. Observed baseline = 100% success invalidates that assumption and makes the confirmatory null outcome uninformative about GVR benefits outside the tested conditions. Operational implications. Within well-scoped, template-like intents in an emulated environment and for this model, LLM-only generation can produce verifier-acceptable outputs; however, guarded architectures remain essential where (a) tasks are open-ended, (b) the validator is weaker or less comprehensive, (c) models are more stochastic or untrusted, or (d) production hardware semantics exceed emulator coverage. Reproducibility. All artifacts, code, provider traces, validator traces, and hashes are published in the execution_manifest (see execution/* paths and SHA-256 manifest entries).
sections.conclusion: We report a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation comparing LLM-only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline on 200 stratified intent-to-configuration tasks in a deterministic Mininet emulation using gpt-5-mini. Both arms produced verifier-accepted configurations on every confirmatory task (200/200), yielding a paired difference of 0.00 (95% CI [0.00, 0.00]). The result reflects the constrained scope and the preregistered shared-initial-candidate semantics; it does not imply that GVR is unnecessary for broader, more stochastic, adversarial, or production settings. We publish the full preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, validator traces, deterministic analysis, and all hashes (see execution_manifest). Future work should expand model diversity, richer protocols and device families, and broader verifier coverage to map the conditions under which GVR provides operational gains.

limitations: Emulation and synthetic task scope: confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor-inspired templates executed in a Dockerized Mininet emulator; external validity to production devices, vendor firmware differences, and hardware bugs is limited.
Single-model evaluation: only gpt-5-mini was tested in the preregistered confirmatory experiment; results do not generalize across models or model families.

Shared-generation preregistered semantics: generation_semantics was preregistered as "shared_initial_candidate" so each task used one LLM candidate that both arms evaluated; consequently, when no repair was invoked baseline and guarded responses were identical (identical response hashes observed for all 200 tasks; examples: task-000001 hash f8de4d6e...; task-000002 hash ae967f70...; see execution/execution_manifest.json for full list), which materially affects interpretation of a null paired difference.

Validator coverage constraints: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforced syntax normalization, ordering/atomicity/workflow constraints (e.g., "must be down for MTU/VLAN change"), and emulated reachability/policy probes inside Mininet; its rule set is finite and may not cover richer device semantics, stateful middleboxes, or production-specific behaviors (transformation manifest: execution/transformation_manifest.json, SHA-256 7925b8f25adbb269...).

Preregistered power assumption violated: the confirmatory power calculation targeted detecting a 10 percentage-point absolute reduction; observed baseline success = 200/200 (100%); therefore the planned power analysis is not informative and the null confirmatory outcome reflects the tested scope rather than a general absence of GVR benefit.

Contamination detection limits: automated token-overlap contamination checks (pre-registered threshold ≥80%) flagged 0 confirmatory tasks; however undiscoverable overlap with model pretraining data cannot be fully excluded.
